principles: A root constrains lexical relationships but does not determine contextual sense.
Construction, syntax, immediate context, and intra-Quranic contrast outrank root imagery.
Render settled religious vocabulary plainly when that is what the context conveys.
A default is never a universal substitution; context selects among recorded senses.
Do not turn editorial rationale into a historical note for readers.

senses.condition: Form IV verb with bi- introducing God, the Last Day, scripture, messengers, signs, or another propositional object
Form IV verb with li- introducing a person or testimony
Active participle naming members of the believing community
Only where the syntax and immediate context concern safety, security, entrusting, or giving assurance

entries.prohibited_default: Do not render belief constructions as entrusting oneself unless the context independently activates trust or security.

senses.condition: The fixed expression yawm al-dīn and eschatological repayment contexts
senses.rendering: the Day of Judgment; the Day of Reckoning

senses.condition: A ruler's or God's binding order in an immediate legal context, including 12:76 and 24:2
A named communal, doctrinal, or worship system
The passage foregrounds service, obedience, or exclusive devotion rather than a named system

entries.prohibited_default: Do not use 'way of allegiance' or 'debt' as a global rendering.

senses.condition: All Quranic occurrences
senses.rendering: unlawful sex; one who has unlawful sex

entries.prohibited_default: Do not use 'fornication' as the sole English term; modern English often limits it to unmarried people and can exclude adultery.

senses.condition: A revealed text or recognized sacred writing
A written account, register, or personal record
A human letter or document, such as 27:28
Passive kutiba with ʿalā in a legal obligation formula
The passage concerns the physical act of writing

entries.prohibited_default: Do not force 'the Writ' or 'written for you' where writing is lexicalized as scripture, record, decree, or obligation.

senses.condition: God communicates revelation to a prophet or the passage names revealed content
Divine direction to a non-prophetic recipient, including Moses' mother or the bees
Human gestural or covert communication

entries.prohibited_default: Do not flatten prophetic revelation to generic 'communication'.

senses.condition: Divine-name and predicate uses

entries.prohibited_default: An intensive form does not by itself license the universal quantifier 'all'.

senses.condition: The hapax at 81:4

entries.prohibited_default: Do not reduce the noun to generic pregnant camels.

senses.condition: The hapax passive participle at 81:8
senses.rendering: the girl buried alive; the female infant buried alive

entries.prohibited_default: Do not omit the live-burial content; 'the buried girl' is materially incomplete.

senses.condition: The mountain similes at 70:9 and 101:5

entries.prohibited_default: Generic 'wool' may lose the lexical color component; preserve it where the mountain image is translated.

senses.condition: The concrete royal object at 38:34 or the divine kursiyy at 2:255

entries.prohibited_default: Do not silently merge kursiyy with ʿarsh, the Quran's other throne term. If 'throne' is chosen for clarity at 2:255, flag the lexical distinction in a note.

senses.condition: The inheritance formula at 4:11

entries.prohibited_default: The masculine plural and its inclusive legal application are materially disputed here; do not choose gender-neutral 'siblings' without a note.

senses.condition: The context clearly denotes the act or process
The context clearly denotes creatures or created things
senses.rendering: creation; created beings; what was created

senses.condition: Both the process and result readings remain live

entries.prohibited_default: Do not add 'act of' unless the context excludes created things.

senses.condition: The lexicalized contrast with the life to come
Only where the passage itself activates spatial nearness

entries.prohibited_default: Do not force 'this nearer life' into ordinary lexicalized occurrences.

senses.condition: Proper-name uses

entries.prohibited_default: Do not use opaque 'Gehenna' in the reader text unless the proper-name distinction is materially relevant and explained.

senses.condition: The established ritual practice

entries.prohibited_default: Do not derive an English meaning from a proposed racehorse metaphor; do not use the awkward label 'prayer-rite' when plain English works.

senses.condition: A warning, threat, judgment, legal boundary, retaliation rule, or direct command is active
senses.rendering: fear God; be on guard; guard yourselves

senses.condition: The form describes a person's stable character or names a pious class without an active warning
senses.rendering: mindful of God; awareness of God

senses.condition: The clause explicitly names what is guarded against or what protection is requested

entries.prohibited_default: Do not flatten warning, legal, threat, or judgment contexts into the signature phrase 'mindful of God.' Context selects force; the root alone does not.

senses.condition: The syntax denotes an act, occasion, or portion of recitation
Title-like reference to the revealed corpus

entries.prohibited_default: Do not force 'the Recitation' into title-like contexts or 'the Quran' into ordinary verbal-noun contexts.

QAC-WQY.source: Quranic Arabic Corpus, root W-Q-Y concordance and morphology
QAC-WQY.observation: The family includes direct protection, imperatives, purpose clauses, participles, and character descriptions; construction and context determine English force.

PILOT-TAQWA-FORCE.observation: All 34 W-Q-Y morphology segments in the 300-ayah pilot were mechanically enumerated and context-classified before force-only corrections.

QAC-9-61.source: Quranic Arabic Corpus, 9:61 word-by-word and grammar
QAC-9-61.observation: One verse contrasts yuʾminu bi-llāh with yuʾminu lil-muʾminīn, demonstrating construction-sensitive senses.

QAC-24-2.observation: The legal passage contains dīn Allāh, tuʾminūna bi-llāh, al-muʾminīn, and zānī/zāniyah in one immediate context.

QAC-12-76.observation: Dīn al-malik denotes the king's governing law or system in the immediate legal narrative.

QAC-DYN.source: Quranic Arabic Corpus, root D-Y-N concordance
QAC-DYN.observation: The concordance separately glosses judgment, law, religion, worship, and debt-related forms by context.

QAC-2-183.observation: Passive kutiba with ʿalaykum introduces a binding fasting obligation and is glossed 'is prescribed'.

QAC-KTB.source: Quranic Arabic Corpus, root K-T-B concordance
QAC-KTB.observation: The root occurs in literal writing, scripture, record, and prescribed-obligation contexts.

QAC-81-4.observation: The comparison records full-term or ten-month pregnant she-camels as the specific referent of al-ʿishār.

QAC-81-8.observation: The feminine passive participle al-mawʾūdah is glossed as the female infant buried alive.

LEX-IHN.source: Classical Arabic lexicon aggregation, entry ʿ-h-n
LEX-IHN.observation: The collected lexicon entries distinguish ʿihn as dyed or colored wool.

QURAN-70-9.observation: The same mountain-to-ʿihn comparison occurs here.

QURAN-101-5.observation: Mountains are compared with al-ʿihn al-manfūsh.

QAC-2-255-KRSY.observation: The verse contains kursiyyuhu, a noun distinct from the Quran's ʿarsh vocabulary.

QURAN-38-34.observation: The Quran's other kursiyy occurrence denotes Solomon's seat.

QURAN-ARSH-CONTRAST.observation: The Quran elsewhere uses ʿarsh for throne; keeping the lexical distinction avoids collapsing two terms.

QURAN-4-11.observation: The inheritance formula uses ikhwah without an explicit feminine form.

LEGAL-IKHWA-DISPUTE.observation: Whether the masculine plural is translated as brothers or inclusively as siblings is material in this legal context and requires explicit review.

LANE-AMN.source: Edward William Lane, Arabic-English Lexicon, root A-M-N
LANE-AMN.observation: The entry distinguishes security, trust, belief, and faith senses rather than reducing Form IV to one root gloss.

LANE-DYN.source: Edward William Lane, Arabic-English Lexicon, root D-Y-N
LANE-DYN.observation: The entry records obedience, religion, religious law, judgment, rule, and debt-related senses.

LANE-ZNY.source: Edward William Lane, Arabic-English Lexicon, zān/zina entry
LANE-ZNY.observation: The sexual-offense term is broader than the unmarried-only sense that modern English often assigns to fornication.

LANE-QRA.source: Edward William Lane, Arabic-English Lexicon, root Q-R-ʾ
LANE-QRA.observation: The entry records both recitation/readings and title-like use for the revealed corpus.

QURAN-20-13.observation: Divine speech to Moses names what is revealed.

QURAN-42-13.observation: Waḥy is used for revelation to Muhammad in a prophetic sequence.

QURAN-16-68.observation: The same verb describes divine direction to bees.

QURAN-28-7.observation: The same verb describes divine inspiration to Moses' mother.

QURAN-19-11.observation: The same root describes Zechariah signaling to his people.

QURAN-36-79.observation: Khalq can leave act/result scope unresolved without contextual forcing.

QURAN-7-54.observation: Creation language can denote the created order as well as the act.

QURAN-11-15.observation: Al-ḥayāt al-dunyā functions as the established contrastive label for present life.

QURAN-18-46.observation: Al-ḥayāt al-dunyā functions as the established contrastive label for present life.

MORPH-INTENSIVE-POLICY.observation: Morphological intensity does not itself assert universal scope.

CLARITY-POLICY.observation: Prefer immediately understood reader English when no material semantic distinction is lost.

SETTLED-RELIGIOUS-TERM-POLICY.observation: Use plain established English for a settled ritual term rather than manufacturing a root metaphor.
